title: Why We Built Dancify: A Practice Diary Made of Footage
headline: Why we built a dance practice app with no feed and no scores
h1: Why we built a dance practice app with no feed and no scores
dek: Dancers film everything and find nothing. Here's why we built Dancify around the camera and a calendar of frames, the decisions behind it, what we left out on purpose and where we're taking it.
description: The story behind Dancify: why dancers' practice videos get lost, the six decisions that shaped the app, what we left out on purpose, and what comes next.

faq.a: Dancify is designed and built by AppRise Ventures Oy, a small company in Espoo, Finland. The app is available for iPhone and iPad, in English, German, Finnish, Spanish, French and Japanese.

faq.q: What's free in Dancify, and what's Premium?
faq.a: Recording, the calendar and timeline, notes, tags, milestones, the practice tools (count-in, reference video, A–B loop, counts), the video editor and iCloud sync are free. Dancify Premium, yearly with a one-week free trial or monthly, adds progress reel export, side-by-side compare and the pose guide.

faq.q: Do I need an account to use Dancify?
faq.a: No. There's no account, no sign-in and no profile. Your videos and diary stay on your device, or in your own private iCloud if you turn sync on. The App Store privacy label is Data Not Collected.

faq.q: Does Dancify use AI to score my dancing?
faq.a: No. Dancify doesn't score or rank dancing. The optional pose guide (Premium) uses Apple's Vision framework on your device to draw lines over shoulders, hips and balance so you can see your alignment; nothing is uploaded and nothing is graded.

faq.q: Why doesn't Dancify have a social feed or streaks?
faq.a: Practice footage is meant to be unfinished, and rest days are part of training. A feed would make you film for an audience, and streaks would make a rest day feel like failure. You can still export and share any take or reel when you choose.
No. Dancify is built natively for iPhone and iPad running iOS or iPadOS 26 or later, including the iPhone Duo. There's no Android or web version.
